extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants (including pro se applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on who may represent applicants/owners before the USPTO, how powers of attorney must be executed and recognized, signature/certification obligations for papers filed, and limited/exceptional recognition of non-registered individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO cannot aid in selection of patent practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office cannot aid in the selection of a patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may suggest that a pro se applicant employ a registered patent practitioner if patentable subject matter appears disclosed and the applicant appears unfamiliar with proper preparation and prosecution, but must not suggest employment if the application appears to contain no patentable subject matter. Use form paragraph 4.10 when suggesting use of a practitioner. Provide applicant with listing at www.uspto.gov/FindPatentAttorney or OED contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must be represented by a registered practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A juristic entity (e.g., organizational assignee) must be represented by a patent practitioner even if the juristic entity is the applicant; non-juristic applicants may prosecute pro se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.31. Pro se applicants presenting papers make the certifications under 37 CFR 11.18(b) and may be subject to sanctions under 37 CFR 11.18(c) for violations. See MPEP §§ 402.03 and 410 for related signature/certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'patent practitioner' and design practitioner limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent practitioner means a registered patent attorney or registered patent agent under §11.6. An attorney or agent registered under §11.6(d) may only act as a practitioner in design patent applications or other design patent matters or proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patent practitioners registered under 11.6(d) can only be listed on powers of attorney in design patent matters; practitioners under 11.6(a)-(c) may practice in all patent matters including design. Customer number practice including design practitioners is limited to design matters. See MPEP § 1502.02 and §403.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney — who may be named as representative
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney may only name as representative: (1) one or more joint inventors (§1.45); (2) those registered patent practitioners associated with a Customer Number; (3) ten or fewer patent practitioners, stating the name and registration number of each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a power names more than ten patent practitioners, it must be accompanied by a separate paper indicating which ten are to be recognized by the Office; otherwise the Office will not recognize more than ten patent practitioners of record (except for the Customer Number or joint inventor exceptions). See 37 CFR 1.32(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney form and content requirements (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney must be in writing, name one or more representatives in compliance with 1.32(c), give the representative power to act on behalf of the principal, and be signed by the applicant for patent or the patent owner (with differences pre- and post-September 16, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, signature must be by applicant for patent (37 CFR 1.32(b)(4)) or patent owner where applicable. For pre-AIA applications (before Sep 16, 2012), different signature rules apply (applicant or assignee of entire interest). See MPEP §402.02(a) and §402.02(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration number controls recognition (name/number mismatch)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the name on the power of attorney does not match the name associated with the registration number in OED records, the Office recognizes the person associated with the registration number because the Office enters the registration number, not the name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a wrong registration number is provided, a new power of attorney will be required to correct the error. Examiners should be aware that Office recognition follows the registration number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineffective power of attorney — not registered or not inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney given to a person who is neither registered to practice before the USPTO for the type of application nor named as the inventor/joint inventor in the application is ineffective; the appointment is void ab initio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a POA is ineffective, the correspondence address of record will not be the ineffective POA address; the Office of Patent Application Processing will select an official correspondence address per MPEP §403.01. Use form paragraph 4.09 to notify applicant that the attorney/agent is not registered. Examiners should check Patent Data Portal and OED to determine recognition status before using form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of attorney naming firms and the ten-practitioner limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Powers of attorney naming firms will not be recognized. A power naming more than ten practitioners will only be entered if Customer Number practice is used or accompanied by a separate paper identifying which ten to recognize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a POA is not entered due to naming >10 practitioners, a copy should be refiled with the separate paper as set forth in 37 CFR 1.32(c)(3). PTO/AIA/82 Part C may be used to appoint up to 10 practitioners by name and registration number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition in patent matters (37 CFR 11.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals not registered under §11.6 may, upon showing necessary or justifiable circumstances and good moral character and reputation, be given limited recognition by the OED Director to prosecute specified patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition does not extend beyond specified applications and is not granted to those who have passed the registration exam while their registration application is pending. Immigration-based limited recognition may be granted consistent with authorized employment/training and subject to visa/immigration rules; it terminates if the individual ceases authorized status or residence. Limited recognition may permit prosecuting international applications under conditions (PCT Art.49, Rule 90, §1.455). Persons with limited recognition are considered practitioners under 11.1 and may file certain documents (e.g., POA under 1.32(b)(4), access to application under 1.14(c), changes of correspondence address under 1.33(a), terminal disclaimer 1.321(b)(1), express abandonment request 1.138(b)), but remain subject to restrictions in their grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only authorized practitioners may represent others (37 CFR 11.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only practitioners registered under §11.6; individuals given limited recognition under §11.9(a) or (b) or §11.16; or individuals admitted pro hac vice per §§41.5(a) or 42.10(c) may represent others before the Office in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibits unregistered individuals from prosecuting others' patent applications except as explicitly allowed by limited recognition or pro hac vice admission. Persons granted limited recognition are subject to temporal, employer, and visa limitations in their grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney in continuing applications (effect and filing copy)
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney from a prior national application for which benefit is claimed in a continuing application may have effect in the continuing application if a copy of the prior power is filed in the continuing application, unless (1) the power was granted by the inventor and (2) the continuing application names an inventor not named in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.32(d) requires that a copy of the prior POA be filed in the continuing application to have effect; the copy must comply with 1.32(b) in the continuing application (e.g., signed by the applicant named in the continuing application). See MPEP §402.02 II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney forms for applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 (PTO/AIA/80,81,82,81A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific USPTO POA forms (PTO/AIA/80, PTO/AIA/81, PTO/AIA/82, PTO/AIA/81A) are available for use in applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, with form-specific content and signature rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTO/AIA/80 for assignees (must be accompanied by 37 CFR 3.73(c) statement when assignee becomes applicant); PTO/AIA/81 for joint inventor-applicants (all joint inventor-applicants must sign); PTO/AIA/82 has Parts A (transmittal), B (POA; must be signed by applicant), and C (optional list of up to 10 practitioners by name and reg. number). Part B cannot be altered after applicant signature; practitioners may complete Part A per-application. PTO/AIA/81A for patents from applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 and must be signed by applicant or current patent owner (with 3.73 compliance if owner signs). Office no longer recommends combined declaration/POA documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney forms for pre-Sept 16, 2012 applications (PTO/SB/80, PTO/SB/81, PTO/SB/81A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before September 16, 2012, use forms PTO/SB/80 or PTO/SB/81; PTO/SB/81A may be used in patents that issued from such applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pre-AIA applications the POA should preferably be signed by the assignee of the entire interest where one exists to avoid client representation issues; if continuation/divisional filed with copy of parent declaration, identify any change in POA that occurred after filing of parent by including most recent POA to ensure correct recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate power of attorney practice eliminated
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective June 25, 2004, the associate power of attorney practice was eliminated; the Office no longer accepts a power of attorney signed by a principal to name an associate power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments of an associate POA filed on or after June 25, 2004 are not accepted. See MPEP §406 and Federal Register revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: POA signature authority for assignees and who may sign
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney must be signed by someone authorized to act on behalf of the assignee-applicant (a person with a title that carries apparent authority or a statement of authorization). A patent practitioner is not authorized to act on behalf of an assignee simply by virtue of authority to prosecute an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assignee who is not the applicant may sign a POA only if the assignee becomes the applicant per 37 CFR 1.46(c), which requires compliance with 37 CFR 3.71 and 3.73. Where an assignee gives practitioner specific authority (organizational resolution), a practitioner may sign certain forms on behalf of the assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements and certifications for papers filed (37 CFR 11.18/1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every paper filed in the Office by a practitioner must bear a personal signature in compliance with §1.4(d) or §2.193(a). By presenting any paper the presenter certifies under 37 CFR 11.18(b) that statements of fact are true, legal contentions are warranted, allegations have evidentiary support or likely will after investigation, denials are warranted, and the paper is not presented for an improper purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of 11.18(b)(2)(i)-(iv) are subject to sanctions under 11.18(c) (e.g., striking the paper, referring to OED, precluding submissions, affecting weight of paper, terminating proceedings). Practitioners may also face disciplinary action. 11.18(b) adopts the substantive requirements of Fed. R. Civ. P. 11(b); practitioners must conduct an 'inquiry reasonable under the circumstances' before presenting papers. 1.4(d)(4)-(5) add that inserted signatures must be authentic and persons filing papers signed by another must have reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted; retain evidence of authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of violating signature/certification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of 37 CFR 11.18(b)(1) may jeopardize validity of the application or resulting patent; violations of 11.18(b)(2)(i)-(iv) may, after notice and opportunity to respond, lead to sanctions including striking the paper, referral to OED, preclusion, affecting weight, or terminating proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions under 11.18(c) are discretionary and may be combined; OED may determine disciplinary action in lieu of or in addition to sanctions. The Office does not routinely review all correspondence for 11.18(b)(2) compliance but will forward files for determination when circumstances warrant (see MPEP §714.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner 'reasonable inquiry' standard and limits (no new duty to search prior art)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 11.18(b)(2) requires an 'inquiry reasonable under the circumstances' (same standard as Fed. R. Civ. P. 11(b)); however, this requirement does not impose a duty on applicant to conduct a prior art search before filing an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amount of investigation required depends on time available and probability that more investigation will yield important evidence (negligence-like standard). The 'reasonable inquiry' requires inquiry into underlying facts when making conclusive statements (e.g., statements about unintentional delay). Practitioners relying on applicant or third-party information will be considered reasonable so long as they have no knowledge of contrary information; practitioners are encouraged to advise clients that provided information must be reliable and not misleading. Failure to perform adequate inquiry in some contexts may lead to sanctions or affect patent enforceability (cases cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions regarding suspended or disbarred practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Any power of attorney given to a practitioner who has been suspended or disbarred by the Office is ineffective and does not authorize the person to practice before the Office or represent applicants/patentees in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners and applicants should verify current recognition status through Patent Data Portal or OED before treating a POA as effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition & international application practice (PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual not registered under §11.6 may, if appointed by an applicant, prosecute an international patent application before the United States International Searching Authority and the United States International Preliminary Examining Authority provided the individual has the right to practice before the national office with which the international application is filed (per PCT Art.49, Rule 90 and §1.455), or before the International Bureau when the USPTO acts as Receiving Office under PCT Rules 83.1 bis and 90.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition for international roles is contingent on the individual's right to practice before the foreign national office and any immigration/employment constraints; see 37 CFR 11.9(c) and MPEP §§1807, 2911 for representation in international applications and design international applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Number practice — recognition of practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney may name those registered patent practitioners associated with a Customer Number; powers that designate all practitioners associated with a Customer Number are recognized (subject to Customer Number practice rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §403 for addition/deletion of practitioners associated with a Customer Number and related correspondence practice. A Customer Number that includes a design patent practitioner can only be used in power of attorney in design patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA signature rules for papers filed (applications filed before Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before September 16, 2012, in the absence of appointment of a registered practitioner, papers must be signed: (1) by all named applicants unless one named applicant has been given a power of attorney to sign on behalf of the remaining applicants and the POA is of record; or (2) if there is an assignee of record of an undivided part interest, by all named applicants retaining an interest and such assignee; or (3) if there is an assignee of the entire interest, by such assignee; or (4) by a registered patent attorney or agent not of record who acts in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These pre-AIA signature requirements derive from pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.32(b) and 1.41(b). The Office suggests that when filing continuations or divisionals with a copy of the parent declaration, applicants should include an updated POA copy if changes occurred after filing of the parent application.
